project_narrative_summary: This project involved BFA (Bowman Foster & Associates) as a subconsultant to GORDON Engineering and IntegriWard LLC to perform an Infrastructure Improvements Analysis (IIA) for the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Advanced Training Center (ATC) in Harpers Ferry, West Virginia. The IIA evaluated the ATC campus's existing utility infrastructure — potable water, fire suppression, irrigation, sanitary sewer, electrical, and communications systems — and developed a phased improvement plan to support the campus's 25-year build-out as defined in the 2017 Area Development Execution Plan (ADEP). BFA's specific scope was the electrical and communications systems analysis. The study identified a significant electrical capacity constraint (the existing 12.5kV Potomac Edison circuit at/near capacity), developed a ductbank mapping of over 63 power manholes/handholes and numerous communications infrastructure nodes, and recommended phased electrical infrastructure improvements costing approximately $4.5 million across five fiscal year windows (FY2022–FY2042). The 95% submission was delivered in May 2021.
